cards.title: The Cost of Delay
cards.insight: Trump's decision to delay Russia sanctions in pursuit of negotiating leverage illustrates how short-term tactical moves can fracture coalitions. Delaying painful measures for future gain often triggers immediate defection from allies who see it as weakness.
cards.takeaway: When postponing a difficult decision, map which stakeholders lose trust immediately vs. those willing to wait for promised results—and build your communication strategy accordingly.

cards.title: Transparency as Liability
cards.insight: Anthropic's alleged secret lobbying to set a 50-death threshold for AI shutdown contradicts its public safety-first positioning. Hidden advocacy undercuts credibility far more than transparent disagreement would.
cards.takeaway: If your values conflict with public statements, acknowledge the tension openly rather than lobby privately—consistency matters more to long-term trust than appearing uniformly righteous.

cards.title: Scale Signals Urgency
cards.insight: Major tech firms' near-total withdrawal from H-1B visa sponsorship (Cognizant zero, Infosys −91%) sends a market signal far louder than any policy statement. Behavioral exits reveal true confidence levels.
cards.takeaway: Watch what decision-makers *do* under pressure, not what they *say*—mass simultaneous exits are a leading indicator of regime risk.

cards.title: Public Backlash as Feedback Loop
cards.insight: French PM Lecornu's partial curfews and Trump's 33% approval rating both show decisions made without broad consensus breeding faster erosion of authority. Early silence often precedes sudden collapse.
cards.takeaway: Build explicit consent mechanisms into major decisions before implementation—waiting for consensus feels slow until mass defection makes reversal impossible.
